procedural_history.originating_court: This case originated in the Supreme Court of India as a Writ Petition (Civil) No. 406 of 2013 under its Civil Original Jurisdiction.
procedural_history.impugned_order: There is no specific order being challenged in this document. The document refers to an Interlocutory Application No. 26542 of 2018 filed within the existing Writ Petition (Civil) No. 406 of 2013. The application seeks directions and declarations regarding the rights and treatment of prisoners sentenced to death.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: There are no High Court proceedings mentioned in this document.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court is currently considering an Interlocutory Application within a Writ Petition related to inhuman conditions in prisons. The Court has requested the Justice Amitava Roy Committee to examine the issues raised in the application in greater depth, alongside the Committee's existing Terms of Reference. The applicant is permitted to assist the Committee.

arguments.issue_text: Whether prisoners sentenced to death have a right to be treated at par with other convicted prisoners and be provided with similar facilities.
appellant_arguments: The applicant, supported by the Amicus Curiae, argued that a convict sentenced to death is entitled to be treated and dealt with like any other convicted prisoner.
The convict is entitled to the opportunity to work on a voluntary basis.

The convict is entitled to other facilities such as participating in educational programmes, vocational training, skill development, and other institutional facilities available to other convicted prisoners.
respondent_arguments: The provided text does not contain any arguments from the respondent.
arguments.court_acceptance: The court did not rule on the merits of the arguments. It left the issue open for consideration by the Justice Amitava Roy Committee.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the solitary, separate, or cellular confinement of prisoners on death row is unconstitutional.
appellant_arguments: The applicant prayed that the solitary confinement of prisoners on death row, or their separate and cellular confinement, be struck down as unconstitutional.
respondent_arguments: The provided text does not contain any arguments from the respondent.
arguments.court_acceptance: The court did not rule on the merits of the arguments. It left the issue open for consideration by the Justice Amitava Roy Committee.

cases.principle: The fundamental rights under Articles 14, 19, and 21 operate within prisons; a separate cell is not different from solitary confinement; and imposing special punitive or harsh restrictions on prisoners requires compliance with natural justice and a right of appeal to a judicial body.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The rights of prisoners as enunciated by the Supreme Court are available to them not only in a particular State but in all the States and Union Territory Administrations across the country.
obiter: The decisions of this Court have quite clearly defined when a prisoner could be said to be on death row and have also taken care of the rights of prisoners on death row as well as those who are a security risk.
Human rights are as much cherished by the State as by the citizen.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found it unnecessary to adjudicate the issues raised in the application regarding the rights of death row prisoners. Instead of ruling on the merits, it left all the issues open for consideration by the Justice Amitava Roy Committee, thereby deferring a decision.
why_appellant_lost: The court explicitly stated, 'We do not think it necessary to go into all the issues raised in the application.'
The court decided to leave the issues open for consideration by the Justice Amitava Roy Committee rather than granting the declarations and directions sought by the applicant.
why_respondent_won: The respondent prevailed because the court declined to rule on the merits of the appellant's application and did not grant the requested relief.
The court's decision to defer the matter to the Justice Amitava Roy Committee meant that the existing prison practices, which the appellant challenged, were not struck down.
policy_considerations: The court reiterated a directive from a previous case that all State Governments must update their prison rules and instructions to align with the Supreme Court's rulings on prison administration and Article 21 of the Constitution, in order to prevent violations of prisoners' rights and reduce litigation.
